page.description: Rescuezilla editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A clonezilla-compatible disk-imaging live system with a graphical interface: back up, restore and clone whole disks and partitions, including images made by Clonezilla.
pros: Graphical front end over partclone, no command line needed.
Reads and writes Clonezilla images, so existing backups stay usable.
Runs from a live USB without installing anything.
SHA-256 checksums are published with each ISO.
cons: Backup and recovery only: it is not a desktop system.
Four Ubuntu-base variants are offered, which is easy to misread.
Restoring to a different disk size needs care with partition layout.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Rescuezilla; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write one ISO to a USB stick with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick. The system runs from the stick and writes images to another drive.
